chunks: And as for what was narrated - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Murram from him who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he was asked about a woman who commanded her son to have intercourse with a concubine belonging to her husband, so he had intercourse with her. He said: 'She is sinful and her son is sinful. And some of these people asked me about this matter, so I said to them: Retain her, for the permissible does not invalidate the permissible.'.

So it does not contradict the first report because in this report there is no indication that she commanded her son to have intercourse with her before the father's penetration or after it. So if that is not explicit in it, and it accommodates both meanings together, we apply it to what we presented earlier, because the first report is detailed and this is general, and the ruling based on the detailed is more worthy than the ruling based on the general.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman commands her son to have intercourse with her husband's concubine?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that when a woman commands her son to have intercourse with her husband's concubine, both she and the son incur sin, establishing that the husband's inherent right (al-halal) does not invalidate the son's distinct sin (al-haram). Shaykh al-Tusi notes that this ruling is specific to the command structure and does not contradict earlier reports, as the permissibility of the husband's act remains intact regardless of the son's liability. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that the validity of one party's right does not automatically absolve another of sin when their actions are evaluated separately.
